posts.headline: You don't need 20% down to buy a home.
points: FHA loans can start at 3.5% down with a 580 credit score.
Eligible veterans can buy with 0% down on a VA loan.

posts.footnote: Every situation is different. Ask a lender what you qualify for.
posts.caption: Think you need 20% down to buy a house? You don't. posts.headline: What closing costs actually are.
points: Usually about 2% to 5% of the loan amount.
They cover the appraisal, title work, lender fees and prepaid taxes and insurance.
Sellers can sometimes help pay them, and your offer is where you ask.
posts.footnote: Your lender gives you the exact numbers up front.
posts.caption: Closing costs catch a lot of buyers off guard, so here's the short version. They're usually about 2% to 5% of the loan amount and cover things like the appraisal, title work, lender fees and prepaid taxes and insurance. The good news: sellers can sometimes help pay them, and your offer is where you ask. Want to know what yours could look like? Message me.

posts.headline: 3 fixes worth doing before you list.
points: Small repairs buyers notice: leaky faucets, loose handles, burnt-out bulbs.
Fresh neutral paint where walls are scuffed.
Curb appeal: trim, mulch and a clean front door.
posts.footnote: Skip big remodels. They rarely pay for themselves.
posts.caption: Thinking about selling? You don't need a big remodel to make a great first impression. Fix the small things buyers notice, like leaky faucets and burnt-out bulbs, freshen up scuffed walls with neutral paint, and give the front of the house some love. Want a walkthrough of what's worth doing for your home? Message me.
